name: io.github.adamson-gh/localbit
title: LocalBit
description: Will this AI model run on your GPU or Mac? Memory needed and estimated or measured speed.

tools.name: check_fit
tools.description: Checks whether one local AI model fits one hardware setup - a graphics card, several identical cards ('2x RTX 3090') or a Mac - and returns the verdict (fits / tight / does_not_fit), memory needed (weights + context cache + overhead) against memory available, and generation speed in tokens per second: measured on LocalBit's test node where it has run that pair, otherwise estimated with a likely range. When it doesn't fit, it says what to change (smaller quantization, shorter context, other hardware); it warns when the context exceeds the model's published maximum. Use this when the user names a model and their hardware. Use suggest_models instead when they only name hardware ('what can I run?'), compare when weighing two options, and list_known first if a name isn't recognised (unknown names return the closest known ones). Every answer includes a citable source_url and the date the data is current as of.

model.description: Model name, e.g. 'Llama 3.1 8B', 'qwen3:30b', 'gpt-oss 20b', or a size like '13B model'. list_known gives exact names.

hardware.description: Graphics card, several cards ('2x RTX 3090') or a Mac ('M2 Pro 32 GB'), or memory like '12 GB card'. list_known gives exact names.

kv_cache.description: Context cache type: f16 (default), q8_0 or q4_0.

tools.name: suggest_models
tools.description: Lists the largest known local AI models that fit on the given hardware at the given context length (default 8,192 tokens), up to 10, biggest first, each with its quantization, memory needed and speed in tokens per second (measured where LocalBit's node has run it, otherwise estimated). min_tokens_per_s drops models slower than that. Use this when the user names only their hardware and asks what they can run; use check_fit to verify one specific model, and compare to weigh two. If nothing fits it says so; unknown hardware returns an error with how to describe it (a card name, memory like '16 GB', or a Mac chip).

hardware.description: Graphics card or computer, e.g. 'RTX 4060', 'M4 Pro', '16 GB'.

min_tokens_per_s.description: Only models at least this fast (estimated).

tools.name: list_known
tools.description: Returns LocalBit's catalog: kind 'models' gives every model with its id, name and parameter count (and active parameters for mixture-of-experts models); kind 'hardware' gives every graphics card and Mac with its id, name and memory. Each entry says whether LocalBit's test node has measured it. Call this first when unsure how to name a model or card, then pass the exact id to check_fit, compare or suggest_models. Sizes not listed still work in those tools ('13B model', '12 GB card', 'M2 Pro 32 GB').

tools.name: compare
tools.description: Compares two options head to head, in one of two modes: two models on the same hardware (give a_model, b_model and a_hardware), or one model on two hardware setups (give a_model, a_hardware and b_hardware). Returns which fits, which is faster (with the ratio), which leaves more memory free and - only where LocalBit's node measured both - which scores higher on its quality check and uses less energy per answer; otherwise it says those are unavailable. context (default 8,192 tokens) applies to both. Use this when the user is choosing between two options; use check_fit for a single model and hardware. Giving neither b_model nor b_hardware returns an error asking for the second option.

b_model.description: Second model (leave out to compare one model on two cards).

b_hardware.description: Second hardware (leave out to compare two models on the same card).

tools.name: node_log
tools.description: Returns the newest measurements from LocalBit's own RTX 3090 test node, newest first (default 10, up to 50): for each model, measured speed in tokens per second at 16K context, quality score (% of 60 script-graded questions right), card memory used, time to read a 3,000-word document, energy per answer, and the date. Use this when the user asks what has actually been tested or measured recently, or wants real results rather than estimates; use check_fit or compare to answer about a specific model and hardware (they include these measurements automatically when they apply).

tools.name: report_issue
tools.description: Sends LocalBit a report that an answer was wrong (it didn't fit, the speed was different, a spec is off) or that a model or card is missing, so it can be corrected. Use this after check_fit, compare or suggest_models gave an answer the user's real experience contradicts. Real results help most: the tokens per second and memory actually seen, the context length and the runtime. Never include names, emails or other personal details - notes are stored as written with emails, numbers and links removed. Returns a confirmation; each call files a separate report, so send it once. Limited to 5 reports a minute.

note.description: What happened, up to 500 characters. No personal details.
